Wrap a fitted hub or koine model as a lens

Source: R/lens_builtin.R
lens_from_fit.Rd

Turns a model somebody has already fitted into a lens the comparison can read. The draws are taken once, at wrap time, and canonicalised: the fit's native parameter names become the hub's canonical tokens – (Intercept), one per fixed-effect term, sigma, and sd_<group> for each random-effect group – with the variance components on the standard-deviation scale whatever the engine stored. That is what lets an INLA lens, a brms lens and the koine lens be compared component by component instead of by position.

Usage

lens_from_fit(fit, name = NULL, n_samples = 1000L, expresses = "linear")

Arguments

fit

A fitted model: a flexybayes_inla fit, a flexybayes_brms fit, or the flexybayes_koine wrapper emit_koine() returns.

name

Single non-empty string naming the lens, or NULL (the default) to name it after the objective – "inla", "brms" or "koine".

n_samples

Number of posterior draws to take. It reaches the engine's sampler on the INLA path, where the draws are generated on demand, and is ignored by backends that already carry every draw they kept.

expresses

Character subset of linear, plateau, threshold and nonmonotone naming the response shapes this parameterisation can express. The default is linear because a fit's expressiveness is a property of the model formula, which this function does not read.

Value

A quorum_lens() whose fit() returns the canonicalised draws, or a quorum_abstention() with reason unsupported_fit (no adapter for the class), lens_abstained (koine stood down, with the nested reason attached), draws_unavailable (the engine could not hand over draws) or draws_malformed (the draws did not form a posterior).

Details

The independence declaration is read off the fit's class rather than asked for, because the caller holding a fitted object cannot be expected to restate what the engine that produced it already determines. An INLA fit declares the Laplace sampler and the INLA objective, a brms fit declares Stan's NUTS sampler and the brms objective, and the koine wrapper declares koine's stacked battery and koine's own objective; all three declare the hub's formula interlingua and the hub's data preparation, which they genuinely do share.

A class no adapter covers, an engine that cannot hand over its draws, and a koine wrapper that already stood down all return a quorum_abstention() rather than a lens. None of the three is a programmer error: they are facts about the fit, and a comparison that receives them can carry on with the lenses it does have.

See also

lens_koine() to fit koine rather than wrap an existing fit, lens_from_draws() for draws that need no adapter at all.

Examples

# An object no adapter covers is declined by name, never guessed at.
a <- lens_from_fit(structure(list(), class = "lm"))
is_quorum_abstention(a)
#> [1] TRUE
a$reason
#> [1] "unsupported_fit"
